---
title: "Testing & Excel parity"
---

How we keep Python outputs aligned with the official LIC-DSF Excel template.

## Run tests

```bash
uv run pytest                          # skips live_excel (Linux CI)
LIC_DSF_EXCEL=1 uv run pytest -m live_excel   # Windows + Microsoft Excel
```

Default `uv run pytest` is Excel-free and uses committed goldens.

## JSON parity cases

Under `data/parity/cases/`, each directory holds:

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `case.json` | Case id, workbook path, cell overlays, probe catalog filters |
| `expected.json` | Oracle-minted probe goldens (`oracle.excel_build` is `cached`, `grapher`, or `live`) |

```bash
uv run pytest tests/test_parity_cases.py
uv run python -m tests.parity.report
```

Equality uses `tests.parity.equality` (`ABS_TOL=1e-6`, `REL_TOL=1e-12`).

## Mint goldens (oracle only — never the Python SUT)

```bash
# Bootstrap / Linux: last-saved cached values from the bundled .xlsx
uv run python -m tests.parity.mint --all --source cached

# Fast proxy oracle (excel-grapher FormulaEvaluator)
uv sync --extra grapher
uv run python -m tests.parity.mint --case template-baseline-output11 --source grapher

# Windows + Excel: live calculate (authoritative for spreadsheet-identity claims)
uv sync --extra excel
LIC_DSF_EXCEL=1 uv run python -m tests.parity.mint --case template-baseline-output11 --source live
```

`grapher` is a proxy oracle (`excel_build: "grapher"`), not Microsoft Excel.
Prefer `live` when publishing identity claims.

Mint never calls the Python SUT. After minting, `case.json` / `expected.json`
carry `oracle.minted_at` and `template_sha`.

Suggested Output 3 overlay inputs:
[`data/parity/OUTPUT_3_INPUT_CATALOG.md`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/data/parity/OUTPUT_3_INPUT_CATALOG.md).

Full mint notes (including WSL → Windows Excel COM):
[`data/parity/README.md`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/data/parity/README.md).

## Legacy CSV compares

Optional side-by-side dumps under `tests/parity/excel_compare/` used by
`tests/test_compare_*.py`. Prefer JSON parity for new coverage.

## Geometry tables vs thin panels

User-facing demos usually show thin panels (`external_dsa_panel`, …). Full
Excel-geometry tables (`output_11_table`, `output_31_table`, …) are the
parity surfaces compared to live Excel row layouts.
